clue.text: Engineer has trick to get three-legged stand shortened

parts.note: to con is to trick, here as a noun: a con

indicators.note: shortened says the stand's word loses its final letter

parts.note: a trivet is a three-legged stand for a pot or kettle

explanation.surface: An engineer uses a trick to get a wobbly three-legged stand cut down to size.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shortened' clips the last T from TRIVET, leaving TRIVE.
explanation.definitionFit: Verb synonyms: to engineer an outcome is to devise or bring it about cleverly.

clue.text: Molly sometimes joins this cook

definitions.meaning: Molly can be put before this word to make a verb meaning to pamper
to cook eggs gently in water just below boiling

explanation.surface: Someone called Molly sometimes teams up with this chef.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: a mollycoddle pampers, and the word alone also means to poach eggs gently.

clue.text: Appropriate message for one trying to be religious?

definitions.text: Appropriate message for one trying to be religious?

parts.words: Appropriate message for one trying to be religious?
parts.note: read as two words it is a motto banning wickedness, fitting a beginner in a religious order

explanation.surface: What should one tell someone trying to lead a pious life?
explanation.walkthrough: Split it as NO VICE, a fit motto for someone in religious life.
explanation.definitionFit: Religious term: a probationer in a monastery or convent, before taking vows, is a beginner in that life.

clue.text: I had to be in fantastic scenery — circumstance of living in a particular place?

definitions.text: circumstance of living in a particular place?

indicators.note: to be in says the contraction goes inside the rearranged letters
fantastic says the letters of scenery are wildly rearranged

parts.note: I had contracts to I'd

explanation.surface: Someone surrounded by fabulous scenery wonders about life in that spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fantastic' is the anagram signal and 'to be in' the container; 'I had' contracts as people speak it.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition: having one's home at a given location is a period of residence there.

clue.text: Acquittal comes with very brief sign

parts.note: v is the brief form of very
an indication is a sign

explanation.surface: A not-guilty verdict comes with only a short gesture.
explanation.definitionFit: Legal sense: being cleared of a charge proves one right, so an acquittal clears one's name.

clue.text: Like some potatoes mother placed at front of hut

indicators.note: placed at front of says the mother's word comes first, ahead of the hut's

parts.note: ma is a familiar word for mother
a shed is a simple hut

explanation.surface: Mum puts potatoes of some kind at the front of the garden hut.
explanation.definitionFit: Descriptive example: potatoes are commonly served crushed smooth after boiling, a classic side dish.

clue.text: Collect in a church service

parts.note: mass is a church service, the Eucharist

explanation.surface: Someone takes a collection during a church service.
explanation.definitionFit: Verb synonyms: to gather together or accumulate is to collect.

clue.text: Dire choir if tenor finally goes wrong

indicators.note: goes wrong says the letters given are put into a mistaken order
finally picks the closing letter of the word tenor

explanation.surface: The choir would sound dreadful if its tenor ended up singing off-key.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' gives R, the end of 'tenor'; 'goes wrong' rearranges CHOIR IF R.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: something dreadful or terrible is dire.

clue.text: Muck one's found spread around cells

parts.note: dung is muck, animal manure

indicators.note: spread around says the letters of one's are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: Manure gets spread around the cells.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spread around' gives EONS; 'Muck' is the dung, not a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: underground prison rooms are cells.

clue.text: Coming up with rascal, briefly celebrate

indicators.note: briefly says the rascal's word is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: a devil is a mischievous rascal
to sing is to celebrate in song

explanation.surface: Someone invents something with a cheeky rascal, then they briefly celebrate.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym phrase: coming up with a plan means inventing or devising it.

clue.text: Lord said to be sterile

indicators.note: said signals that the lord's title is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: a baron is a lord, a member of the peerage

explanation.surface: A peer is rumoured to be infertile.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: land or animals unable to produce offspring or crops are sterile, or unfruitful.

clue.text: Boy taken outside church and reprimanded

indicators.note: taken outside says the boy's word goes around the church's letters

parts.note: a lad is a boy
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A boy was led out of church and told off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken outside' is the container signal, not a punishment.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal sense: to lace into someone, or lace them, is to beat or scold them severely.

clue.text: Mischief-maker and fool, I have to be poker-faced

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous little creature
an ass is a fool
I have contracts to I've

explanation.surface: A self-confessed prankster and clown resolves to keep a straight face.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: a poker player hides emotion, so a poker-faced person shows no feeling at all.

clue.text: Abrasive impotence US may show

indicators.note: may show says the letters of impotence and US may be rearranged to reveal something else

explanation.surface: Something harsh, perhaps, that American impotence may reveal.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: volcanic rock used to scrub hard skin is an abrasive.

clue.text: Signal outside a Christian organisation conveys an unwelcoming message

indicators.note: outside says the signal's word sits around the single letter that follows

parts.note: a nod is a signal of the head
a mission is a Christian body spreading the faith

explanation.surface: A sign outside a church charity's building conveys a cold message to visitors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' wraps only the A, giving NOAD.
explanation.definitionFit: Notice wording: a sign telling people they may not enter is hardly a welcome.

clue.text: Canadian city volunteers turning up after request — getting stuck in before long

indicators.note: getting stuck in says the request and volunteers are lodged inside the word for before long

parts.note: soon means before long

indicators.note: after says the volunteers come after the request

parts.note: to ask is to request

indicators.note: turning up says the volunteers' letters are read upwards, in a down clue backwards

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's reserve of volunteer soldiers

explanation.surface: Volunteers show up after a request in a Canadian city and pitch in shortly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning up' reads the volunteers upwards; 'after' orders them; 'getting stuck in' lodges both inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a city in the province of Saskatchewan, in Canada.

clue.text: Start business that limits union power

definitions.meaning: to begin trading is to start a business
a workplace where staff need not join a union, curbing union strength

explanation.surface: A new business is founded on limiting trade union influence.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: launching a store, and an industrial term for a non-closed workplace.

clue.text: Extracts to include Italian literature

indicators.note: to include says the extracts' word takes in the Italian letters

parts.note: to wring is to extract by twisting

explanation.surface: An anthology of extracts includes Italian literature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extracts' is a verb here, as in wringing water out, not passages.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: a body of written works or texts is literature.

clue.text: Practise PE manoeuvring round middle of gym in entertaining performances

indicators.note: round says the rearranged letters go around the central letter of gym
manoeuvring says the letters of practise and PE are moved about
middle of picks the central letter of the word gym

explanation.surface: A gym instructor tells pupils to practise their PE routines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'manoeuvring' gives PARTPIECES, and 'round' puts it about Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: party pieces are the turns someone habitually performs to amuse a gathering.

clue.text: Water gushing in vault

definitions.meaning: a natural source of water rising from the ground
to vault is to leap or jump

explanation.surface: Water gushes in an underground chamber.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: a natural fountain of groundwater, and a leap or bound.

clue.text: Coat in Margaret's luggage facing up

indicators.note: facing up says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A coat is found in Margaret's luggage, folded face up.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a long loose overcoat, originally made in Ireland, often with a cape.

clue.text: Athenian character attempts to absorb holy books — good things to digest

parts.note: nu is a letter of the Greek alphabet, used in Athens

indicators.note: to absorb says the attempts' word takes in the holy books' letters

parts.note: tries are attempts
NT is the New Testament, a set of holy books

explanation.surface: A man from Athens tries to take in scripture, finding it good to digest.
explanation.definitionFit: Descriptive: substances that nourish the body are wholesome things for it to digest.

clue.text: Best possible newspaper bargain

parts.note: i is a British newspaper, offshoot of The Independent
a deal is a bargain

explanation.surface: The newspaper offers the best bargain possible.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: perfect, best imaginable, as in a perfect solution.

clue.text: A quiet chum in shock

parts.note: p (piano) is the musical marking for quiet
a pal is a chum

explanation.surface: A softly spoken friend is in a state of shock.
explanation.definitionFit: Verb synonyms: to horrify or dismay someone is to shock them.

clue.text: Desire shown by warlike invader taking country, destroying lots

parts.note: the Huns were warlike invaders of Europe

indicators.note: destroying says the word for lots is removed from the country

parts.note: Germany is a country
many means lots

explanation.surface: A savage invader seizes a nation, wiping out much of its people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'destroying' takes MANY from GERMANY, leaving GER.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: a craving or longing for something is a desire.

clue.text: Traveller needs a bit of time, holidaymaker leaving university

parts.note: mo is short for moment, a bit of time

indicators.note: leaving says the university letter departs from the holidaymaker

parts.note: a tourist is a holidaymaker

explanation.surface: A traveller needs a brief moment when a student holidaymaker leaves college.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaving' takes U out of TOURIST, giving TORIST.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: someone who drives a car is a road traveller.

clue.text: Old college keeping quiet, as one with elevated status?

indicators.note: keeping says the college's word holds the quiet letters

parts.note: a poly was a polytechnic, a British college type abolished in 1992
sh is a call for quiet

explanation.surface: A former college keeps quiet, like someone who thinks themselves rather grand.
explanation.definitionFit: Adverb sense: acting in a refined, upper-class manner is how someone of high social standing behaves.

clue.text: Youngster could be degenerate while avoiding the extremes

indicators.note: could be says the remaining letters may be rearranged into something new
avoiding the extremes drops the first and last letters of degenerate

explanation.surface: A young person might turn bad, though not to the extreme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'avoiding the extremes' leaves EGENERAT, and 'could be' rearranges it.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: someone aged thirteen to nineteen is an adolescent youngster.
